classification.difficultyReason: Use the hinted diameter to construct a proof linking same-arc angles, Thales's theorem and tangent perpendicularity through a shared complementary angle.

content.prompt: Prove that the angle between a tangent line to a circle and a chord from the point of tangency has the same measure as any inscribed angle that intercepts the same arc as the chord. Hint: Draw the diameter through $O$ and $A$.

spec.description: Tangent at A, chord AB, and two chords from the unlabelled upper vertex. Matching unfilled angle arcs replace the source blue sectors.
spec.mathematics: The tangent is perpendicular to OA. The marked tangent–chord angle and inscribed angle intercept arc AB.
spec.answerVisibility: No diameter, auxiliary labels or proof results are supplied.

answer.short:
$\angle BAC=\angle AEB$.

Draw diameter $AD$; both angles equal $90^\circ-\angle BAD$.
answer.worked:
Label the upper inscribed vertex $E$ and a point on the upper-right tangent ray $C$. Draw diameter $AD$ and join $D$ to $B$.

Angles on the same arc give $\angle AEB=\angle ADB$. Since $AD$ is a diameter, $\angle DBA=90^\circ$ by Thales’s Theorem. Hence
$$\begin{align*}\angle AEB&=\angle ADB\\\angle AEB&=180^\circ-\angle DBA-\angle BAD\\\angle AEB&=180^\circ-90^\circ-\angle BAD\\\angle AEB&=90^\circ-\angle BAD.\end{align*}$$
The radius at $A$ is perpendicular to the tangent, so $\angle DAC=90^\circ$. Therefore,
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=90^\circ-\angle BAD\\\angle BAC&=\angle AEB.\end{align*}$$
Every inscribed angle intercepting the same arc equals $\angle AEB$, proving the result.
